# Leslie Moore

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v2 c10 P46](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0046), [v4 c11 P27](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0027), [v4 c38 P10](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0010)</sub>
- **Origin:** Four Winds (the West farm), Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c11 P28](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0028)</sub>

## Appearance

Leslie is an exceptionally beautiful woman, tall and magnificently proportioned, with an ivory-tinted complexion, sea-blue eyes, and rose-red lips. Her most striking feature is her extraordinary, glowing golden hair, which is wrapped in heavy braids around her head like a coronet and reaches to her feet when let down. She has a graceful, springy carriage, a sweet, musical voice, and an alluring, childishly beautiful laugh when genuinely happy.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046), [v2 c21 P88](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0088), [v4 c5 P8](../source/v04-c05.md#nw-v04-c05-p0008), [v4 c5 P13](../source/v04-c05.md#nw-v04-c05-p0013), [v4 c11 P7](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0007), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c12 P15](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0015), [v4 c16 P11](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0011), [v4 c23 P24](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0024)_

## Personality

Naturally clever, proud, spirited, and passionate, Leslie was deeply warped and embittered by years of relentless tragedy, poverty, and isolation. She kept her inner feelings closely guarded behind a cold, reserved, and sometimes sardonic exterior to protect her raw sensibilities from further hurt. Though prone to dark, brooding moods and intense flashes of envy toward those with happy lives, she is fundamentally generous, deeply loyal, and possesses a rich, imaginative nature that blossoms in the company of true friends. When free of her emotional fetters, she reveals a witty, warm, and joyful disposition.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046), [v2 c21 P29](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0029), [v2 c21 P48](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0048), [v2 c23 P35](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0035), [v4 c10 P65](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0065), [v4 c11 P11](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0011), [v4 c11 P28](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0028), [v4 c17 P6](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0006), [v4 c21 P11](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0011), [v4 c21 P21](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0021), [v4 c21 P28](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0028), [v4 c25 P15](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0015)_

## History

Leslie West grew up in Four Winds, Prince Edward Island, in a home marked by poverty and affection, but her childhood was shattered at age twelve when she saw her brother Kenneth killed in a wagon accident. Two years later, her idolized father committed suicide, a discovery Leslie made herself. She persevered through her grief, earned her teaching license at Queen's Academy, and taught at the Glen St. Mary school. At age sixteen, she was pressured by her mother into marrying Dick Moore to prevent the foreclosure of their homestead. After her mother died, Dick went to sea and disappeared. Four years later, Captain Jim Boyd found a brain-damaged man in Havana whom he identified as Dick, and brought him back. For eleven years, Leslie selflessly nursed this man—who was mentally a child—while running her farm and taking in occasional summer boarders to survive. Upon meeting her new neighbors, Anne and Gilbert Blythe, Leslie initially struggled with bitter envy of their happy home, but soon formed a profound, soul-deep friendship with Anne. When Gilbert suggested that an operation might restore Dick's mental faculties, Leslie courageously agreed and took him to Montreal, where the surgery succeeded. However, the restored man proved to be Dick's double-cousin, George Moore; the real Dick Moore had died of yellow fever years prior in Cuba. Suddenly freed from her tragic plight, Leslie returned to Four Winds and eventually admitted her love for Owen Ford, a writer who had boarder with her that summer.

_Sources: [v4 c5 P8](../source/v04-c05.md#nw-v04-c05-p0008), [v4 c11 P14](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0014), [v4 c11 P16](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0016), [v4 c11 P20](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0020), [v4 c11 P23](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0023), [v4 c11 P25](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0025), [v4 c11 P27](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0027), [v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035), [v4 c21 P11](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0011), [v4 c21 P28](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0028), [v4 c29 P10](../source/v04-c29.md#nw-v04-c29-p0010), [v4 c30 P22](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0022), [v4 c31 P28](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0028), [v4 c33 P9](../source/v04-c33.md#nw-v04-c33-p0009), [v4 c38 P9](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0009)_

## Background by volume

- Daughter of Frank West and Rose Elliott of Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c11 P14](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0014), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015)</sub>
- Deeply attached to her father, who was sickly and shiftless  <sub>[v4 c11 P14](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0014), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c21 P35](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0035)</sub>
- Tragically witnessed her younger brother Kenneth killed in a farm accident at age twelve  <sub>[v4 c11 P16](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0016), [v4 c21 P39](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0039), [v4 c21 P40](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0040)</sub>
- Discovered her father's body after he committed suicide when she was fourteen  <sub>[v4 c11 P20](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0020), [v4 c21 P44](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0044)</sub>
- Attended Queen's Academy and took her teacher's license in one year  <sub>[v4 c11 P23](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0023)</sub>
- Coerced by her mother into marrying Dick Moore at sixteen to save their mortgaged farm  <sub>[v4 c10 P46](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0046), [v4 c11 P25](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0025), [v4 c11 P27](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0027)</sub>
- Nursed an invalid, brain-damaged man for eleven years believing him to be her husband  <sub>[v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035)</sub>

## Quotes

> I had a house of dreams once—but it was a palace... I've always thought it was very lovely here. I—I love it, too.  <sub>[v4 c10 P17](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0017)</sub>

> I suppose I am beautiful... I hate my beauty. I wish I had always been as brown and plain as the brownest and plainest girl at the fishing village over there.  <sub>[v4 c10 P30](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0030)</sub>

> Anne, I never had anything to love since my mother died, except Dick's old dog—and it's so dreadful to have nothing to love—life is so EMPTY—and there's NOTHING worse than emptiness...  <sub>[v4 c21 P11](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0011)</sub>

> I ENVY Anne... and I'd envy her even if she had died! She was a mother for one beautiful day. I'd gladly give my life for THAT!  <sub>[v4 c19 P28](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0028)</sub>

> The rose is the flower of love—the world has acclaimed it so for centuries. The pink roses are love hopeful and expectant—the white roses are love dead or forsaken—but the red roses—ah, Leslie, what are the red roses?  <sub>[v4 c38 P7](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0007)</sub>
